takeaways: Azure SQL Database can call external REST APIs directly, so the database can trigger alerts, enrich data with AI and integrate with services without extra application code.
Secure these integrations with firewalls, least privilege, dedicated users, masking and encryption, and store API secrets in database credential objects instead of in procedures.
In the cloud, performance tuning directly lowers cost, and Fabric mirroring offers a near real-time path to BI without hand-built ETL pipelines.
hook: Most teams still treat Azure SQL as passive storage behind the application. In this interview, Dirceu Resende shows data engineers and architects how Azure SQL Database can call REST APIs, automate workflows and support AI with vector search. You learn where this simplifies your architecture and how to keep it secure and performant.
